biggest_catch: You must own the appliance and be a Potomac Edison electric customer in Maryland — renters recycling a landlord's unit don't qualify. Limits apply per household, and the check takes up to six weeks after pickup.
catches: You must own the appliance and be a Potomac Edison electric customer.
Appliances must be in working condition.
The rebate check is mailed within six weeks — not instant.
Limits apply on the number of appliances per household.
Room ACs and dehumidifiers qualify, but amounts differ by appliance type ($100 vs $50).

c1.evidence: Potomac Edison is a FirstEnergy operating company; the program page is on firstenergycorp.com.

c2.evidence: Official FirstEnergy/Potomac Edison appliance turn-in page states: $100 for a working refrigerator or dehumidifier; $50 for a freezer, room air conditioner, or mini refrigerator; check mailed within six weeks.

c3.evidence: Free pickup; no enrollment or participation fee.

c4.evidence: Official page states the check is mailed within six weeks of pickup.

eligibility: Potomac Edison electric customer (Maryland) who owns the appliance being recycled. Appliance must be working. Household limits apply.

steps: Confirm you are a Potomac Edison electric customer and you own the old appliance.
Check the appliance works (refrigerator/dehumidifier = $100; freezer, room AC, or mini fridge = $50).
Schedule the free pickup through the appliance turn-in program page.
Have the working appliance ready on pickup day.
Receive your rebate check in the mail within six weeks.
timing: Check mailed within six weeks after pickup.
